bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang out as CEO — leadership crisis, DOJ probe, China chip scandal coalesce
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned/was ousted as NVIDIA CEO with Colette Kress named interim CEO; stock fell 14% intraday before recovering to -4.3%, erasing ~$600B in market cap. Core concerns: Kress will reduce balance sheet commitments to ecosystem (neoclouds, startups), DOJ antitrust probe directly targeting NVDA, and ~240k AI chips allegedly diverted to China via Singapore cloud partners. Goldman cuts PT to $220 from $300 (maintains Buy, citing execution/cultural risk over 12-24 months); 1,600+ employees petitioned board for reinstatement; Trump called Huang. NVDA earnings still on track for 11/17.

bullets.title: NVDA: Bears vs. Bulls — valuation, semis read-through, and AI demand context
bullets.body: Wolfe sees NVDA as 65.5% upside to $275 PT at 10.6x FY2 P/E (65% discount to 5-yr avg), with AI inference demand still above supply; CEO departure 'already embedded in valuation.' Michael Burry published bearish piece titled 'Say It Ain't So - NVIDIA on Fire.' JPM flags positive directional bias with capped near-term upside into earnings; recommends Mar-27 115%-130% KO calls at 0.77%.

bullets.title: NVDA: AMD +6%, AVGO +5.5% as beneficiaries of leadership vacuum; neoclouds NBIS -17%, CRWV -7%
bullets.body: AMD and AVGO rallied as custom-chip share gain beneficiaries on NVDA CEO transition. NBIS fell 17% and CRWV fell 7% on loss of perceived Nvidia financing backstop — Jensen's personal relationships underpinned capacity pre-purchases and supplier commitments to neoclouds. China-exposed names (BABA -7%, GDS -11%) also fell on remote-access chip control rules.

bullets.title: NBIS: Q3 beats across the board but FY26 revenue guided to low end on Vineland delays
bullets.body: Nebius Q3 revenue $980.8M beat FactSet $907.2M; adj. EBITDA $465.8M vs. $351.8M est.; gross margin 77.6% vs. 71.3% est. GPU pricing up >20% q/q; annual contract value per MW exceeded $25M. FY26 revenue guided to low end of $3.0–3.4B range due to Vineland power transition delays pushing revenue to H1'27; FY26 capex raised to ~$27B. FY27 guidance $12–13B revenue, $40–45B capex. Customer prepayments now cover >100% of Q3 capex. Consensus 65% buy, avg. target $283.90 (~121% upside).

bullets.title: CSCO: Big beat/raise on AI hyperscaler surge; FY27 AI revenue target raised to $9B
bullets.body: Cisco Q1 EPS $1.40 vs. $1.33 est.; revenue $18.52B vs. $18.12B. FY27 revenue guide raised to $74.8–75.8B (+$2.5B, of which $1.5B from AI); FY27 EPS raised to $5.47–5.53 from $5.05–5.11. AI hyperscaler revenue target doubled to $9B (12% of FY27 vs. 6% FY26). Stock pulled back ~4% on order deceleration (21% vs. ~30%+ expected) and GM headwinds from hardware mix. KeyBanc OW, $135 PT; Citi Buy, PT cut to $120 on lower multiple.

bullets.title: AMAT: Beat-and-raise; sees 2027 WFE growth >30%, expects to outperform market
bullets.body: Applied Materials Q4 EPS $4.16 vs. $4.06 est.; revenue $10.41B vs. $10.30B. Q1 guidance: EPS $4.35±$0.20 (vs. $4.24 est.), revenue $11.1B±$500M (vs. $10.85B est.). Management guides 2027 WFE growth at least 30% with AMAT outperforming; Semiconductor Systems Q1 at $8.7B vs. $8.46B est. CY26 semi revenue tracking >40%. Citi and RBC maintain Buy, PTs ~$580–600 (cut from prior $600–670 on peer multiple compression).

bullets.title: CSCO/NVDA/AMAT read-through: Data center capex cycle macro note flags 2028-29 cliff risk
bullets.body: PSC Macro warns data center construction boom peaks 2028–2029 after healthy run through 2027; capex contributing ~2ppts to GDP now but cooling sharply in 2029. Steep drop in announcements threatens tech equipment demand and hyperscaler free cash flow during Fed tightening cycle. Current demand described as robust with moratoriums likely to delay builds, not cancel (only 2–4% cancellation risk).

bullets.title: HUBS: Co-founder Brian Halligan returns as CEO — broadly viewed as sentiment positive
bullets.body: HubSpot announced co-founder Brian Halligan returns as CEO immediately, replacing Yamini Rangan, in what the company describes as a 're-founding.' CTO Duncan Lennox promoted to President of Product; CFO Kate Bueker retiring Feb 2027. Company reaffirmed Q4 and FY26 guidance. JPM and RBC view the leadership change positively, citing expected improvements in AI monetization path (seats + credits model) and expansion rate pressures; Jefferies notes Halligan is broadly respected by investment community.

bullets.title: FOXA: Morgan Stanley resumes at Overweight, Top Pick; $90 PT on Roku synergies and 20% FCF CAGR
bullets.body: MS resumes Fox Corp at Overweight, elevating to Top Pick with $90 PT (~30% upside). Roku deal accelerates EBITDA growth to high-single/low-double digits; $400M+ cost synergy opportunity and $500M–1B revenue synergies not in base case. Targets ~20% FCF/share CAGR to FY30, with path to $8–10 FCF/sh. Fox+Tubi+TRC garners 10%+ monthly US TV viewership. FOXA +2% in premarket.

bullets.title: CVNA: Prime ABS deal signals Q/Q GoS margin expansion ~90bps; JPM bullish
bullets.body: Carvana's 2026-P4 prime ABS deal priced at $1.1B (upsized to $1.5B) with APRs up 88bps Q/Q; excess spread ~5.2% (up ~40bps Q/Q), implying ~90bps higher GoS margin vs. August deal. Average FICO stable at 704; CNL assumptions unchanged ~3%. JPM models Other GPU up Q/Q vs. prior estimate of -$100; prime ABS is ~30% of total monetization routes.

bullets.title: MSFT: Global Outlook/Teams/Copilot outage; services recovering, stock -1.3% premarket
bullets.body: Microsoft suffered widespread 365 outage (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot) affecting millions globally; root cause under investigation with no evidence of malicious activity. As of 8am ET, broader improvements in North America and sustained improvements in Europe. MSFT stock -1.3% premarket. Cybersecurity names rallied on spillover demand: CRWD +2.3%, ZS +2.3%, NET +1.1%.

bullets.title: GOOGL: JPM bullish on Gemini 4 Hydrogen; TPUs 'superior to GPUs,' direct NVDA challenger
bullets.body: JPM Tech Sketch highlights Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen release as a clear relative winner vs. NVDA, with TPUs cited as superior to GPUs. Gemini task automation expanding to 100+ apps, becoming direct META Muse competitor. Hedgeye flags GOOGL IV at -25% discount — 'ridiculously complacent' into ongoing QQQ drawdown.

bullets.title: AVGO: Wolfe top pick in AI compute with 37% upside; Rothschild downgrades — mixed signals
bullets.body: Wolfe Research sees AVGO as best risk/reward among AI compute names with $500 PT (37.2% upside), trading at 12% discount to 5-yr avg; completed significant financing round to support Anthropic's CY27 purchases. Opposing view: Rothschild & Co Redburn downgrades AVGO (stock -2.2% premarket). AMD and AVGO both seen as NVDA market share beneficiaries per GS and UBS.

bullets.title: SMCI: DOJ probe reported alongside NVDA/Megaspeed investigation; stock -13%
bullets.body: DOJ is pursuing separate investigations into Supermicro (SMCI) and Megaspeed, focused on Alice Huang's involvement; probe was transferred to DOJ last year per NY Times. No indication of criminal charges against Huang at this stage. SMCI fell 13% on the news alongside NVDA's leadership turmoil.

bullets.title: TLN: 750MW 7-year capacity deal adds ~$100M/yr revenue; Wells Fargo bullish on cash flow conversion
bullets.body: Talen Energy signed a 750MW, 7-year capacity agreement with LT pricing exceeding PJM auction outcomes, adding ~$100M annually. Wells Fargo views the deal as advancing TLN's strategy to convert PJM capacity fundamentals into contracted cash flows at high margins.

bullets.title: VRT: 60% dividend increase; +2.1% premarket; GS flags 44% EPS downside risk in adverse AI scenario
bullets.body: Vertiv announced a 60% dividend increase, sending shares up 2.1% in premarket. Goldman Sachs cautions that EMS/power names including VRT carry greater earnings risk from AI infrastructure exposure — in a 45% AI capex downside scenario, GS models FY28 EPS down 44% for VRT (vs. 63% FLEX, 58% JBL).

bullets.title: OKLO: Signs uranium supply contracts with Centrus; SMR sector watch
bullets.body: Oklo signed uranium supply contracts with Centrus Energy with deliveries expected to begin in 2029, advancing its fuel supply chain ahead of reactor deployments.

bullets.title: DLR: MS bullish on GMG/NXT JV; addresses Australia gap ahead of #6 global DC market by 2030
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley highlights DLR's 50/50 JV with Goodman Group (GMG.AX) taking a 9.9% stake in NXT (~300MW installed, ~2GW pipeline). The deal addresses DLR's minimal Australia presence (~50MW, ~3% share) while leveraging GMG's local expertise and third-party capital — reducing DLR balance sheet burden. Australia expected to be world's sixth-largest DC market by capacity by 2030.

bullets.title: U (Unity): Piper reiterates OW, $72 PT as top pick; Vector showing broad-based AI and ad demand
bullets.body: Piper Sandler reiterates Unity as top pick with Overweight and $72 PT; Vector platform showing broad-based growth with healthy ad demand; AI tools opportunity for game creation identified as incremental catalyst.

bullets.title: OpenAI cyber expansion threatens PANW, CRWD in VM and pen-testing markets
bullets.body: OpenAI launched 'Daybreak Red Team' and 'Daybreak Defense Factory' products competing directly with vulnerability management vendors (TENB, QLYS) and AI security readiness services from PANW and CRWD. Frontier AI labs are strategically expanding into cybersecurity with potential moves into the AI SOC market, posing a competitive threat to specialist vendors.
